title: The Ramadan Raids
summary: Eve-of-Eid editorial framed as the annual post-Ramadan operational stocktake, set in devotional language about combining fasting, prayer, and combat across the holy month. Enumerates the theatres of the 1447 AH 'Ramadan raids' as the wilayat of West Africa, Central Africa, the Sahel, Mozambique, and the Levant. Claims the mujahideen intensified attacks across the final ten nights of Ramadan in commemoration of the Battle of Badr, and that the Levant front responded to the call to inghimas operations against the soldiers of the tyrant. Treats the synchronisation of attacks across distant theatres against ostensibly distinct armies as evidence of a single global enemy, explicitly aligning 'the tyrants of Damascus' with 'the tyrants of Nigeria' as equivalent target sets. Cites the hadith of al-Ta'ifa al-Mansura to frame the continuity of jihad as a divine promise that no laggard can interrupt. Closes by exhorting the mujahideen to carry operational tempo into the Dhu al-Hijjah season and beyond.
keyClaims: The 1447 AH Ramadan raids were conducted across the IS wilayat of West Africa, Central Africa, the Sahel, Mozambique, and the Levant.
Operations intensified across the final ten nights of Ramadan in commemoration of the Battle of Badr.
Synchronisation of attacks across distant theatres against ostensibly distinct armies is evidence of a single global enemy.
The post-Assad Syrian government is on par with established target sets, from the tyrants of Damascus to the tyrants of Nigeria.
The continuity of jihad is a divine promise and a defining trait of the Victorious Sect.
significanceAssessment: Routine annual product but the geographic claim set is analytically meaningful. The continued elevation of Mozambique alongside the established Sahelian and Lake Chad theatres reflects sustained IS messaging investment in the southern African front. The explicit equation of 'the tyrants of Damascus' with the tyrants of Nigeria normalises al-Sharaa's government as a standing target on par with established adversaries, consistent with the broader anti-HTS editorial campaign.
notes: Gregorian date converted from Hijri 30 Ramadan 1447. Page 3 editorial only.
